discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with the IceCube Neutrino Observatory
motivation: In 2013 IceCube reported the first detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy neutrinos of extraterrestrial origin, opening an entirely new window on the universe. Subsequent observations identified the first neutrino sources: the flaring blazar TXS 0506+056 (2017-2018), the active galaxy NGC 1068 (2022), and neutrino emission from the Galactic plane (2023). Neutrinos are ideal messengers, unaffected by magnetic fields and matter, and they now probe the origin of cosmic rays and the most extreme accelerators in nature. This discovery was made possible by a bold idea: to turn a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a Cherenkov detector. Francis Halzen conceived the concept, championed it through the AMANDA pioneering phase, and led the construction and scientific exploitation of IceCube as Principal Investigator. The citation is sharply defined: the discovery of cosmic high-energy neutrinos, which founded neutrino astronomy beyond the Sun and supernova 1987A.
